lessons.title: Digital Marketing Foundations
lessons.content:
KEY CONCEPTS: Digital marketing promotes products through digital channels, with the defining advantage of measurability — every dollar can be traced to a result, unlike traditional advertising. The core channels: search (SEO/SEM), social media, email, content, display, and affiliate. The marketing funnel online: Awareness → Interest → Consideration → Conversion → Retention/Advocacy. Owned media (your site/list), earned media (shares/PR), and paid media (ads) each play a role. The fundamental shift: from interruption (pushing messages) to permission and attraction (earning attention with value).

WORKED EXAMPLE: A business spends $1,000 on a billboard (traditional) and $1,000 on Google Ads. The billboard gives a vague guess at reach. The Google Ads report shows exactly: 40,000 impressions, 800 clicks, 40 conversions, $25 cost per customer. Digital's measurability turns marketing from guesswork into an optimizable machine — this is its core power.

PRACTICE: 1) Map the digital funnel for a product. 2) Classify three channels as owned/earned/paid. 3) Explain why measurability changes how marketing budgets are allocated.
